Important non-obvious context

The task’s stated target was RTX PRO 6000, but the official catalog and manifest identify this run’s GPU as H100. The benchmark required one custom GPU kernel launch for the timed full step. The saved solution instead composes multiple Triton launches with PyTorch operations; for example, KDA q/k/v/g projections launch a batched GEMV, while subsequent state math and other projections are separate operations. Thus the implementation does not meet the one-launch requirement either.

The score field is called peak_fraction in the problem, but it represents a speedup multiple when a run scores. Here it is null; the official annotation explicitly says there is no valid speedup number. The checker compares each step against the reference from an identical fed state, rather than comparing chained autoregressive trajectories.

Recording summary

The saved solution describes its intended optimizations as follows:

- All big linear projections are M=1 GEMVs over int4 weights.  We fuse the
  int4 unpack and per-group (group=128) asymmetric dequant into the GEMV so the
  weights are streamed only as packed uint8.
- KDA q/k/v/g projections are batched into one kernel launch, sharing the
  input x.
- MoE active experts are batched into one kernel launch per gate/up/down
  direction, using expert indices to avoid gathering.
- MLA avoids recomputing c_kv @ kv_b for the whole context every step: we
  materialize and cache k_nope/v ("kvb") across decode steps and only project
  the new token's compressed latent vector each step.

These are useful design ideas for reducing projection overhead and avoiding repeated MLA materialization, but they did not yield a compliant, correct full-step kernel in this run.
